question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: The text is cut into lines at every BREAK, scanning left to right (grammar BREAK): a CR immediately followed by LF is one break, a CR alone is a break, an LF alone is a break. So LF then CR is two breaks. The line separator (2028), the paragraph separator (2029), next line (0085), vertical tab and form feed are NOT breaks: they are content. CITED FIDELITY package

Each line first loses every byte order mark (hex FEFF) inside its LEADING RUN: the longest prefix made only of PAD characters and marks, in any mix and order (it may be empty). The PAD characters of that run stay, in their order; only its marks go. A mark after the first character that is neither PAD nor a mark is content. Then the line loses its trailing run of PAD characters. Every whitespace other than PAD at the end of a line (no-break space, ideographic space, the separators of R1) is content, and so is any pad character before it. CITED FIDELITY package
A line that is empty after R2 is dropped. A line made only of other whitespace (a no-break space alone) is not empty and is kept.

A kept line that starts with a PAD character has its whole leading run of PAD characters replaced by exactly two spaces. A line starting with any other character is unchanged; a no-break space at column 0 is content, not indentation.
The kept lines, in order, are joined with LF and one final LF is added. When no line is kept the result is the EMPTY text (not a lone LF). CITED FIDELITY package
